description: Every image format Photoshop opens or saves, with bit-depth, layer and transparency support, size limits, the Save/Export dialogs that offer it and the scripting options class; plus the preset, script and plug-in file types the application reads.

tools.name: PSD (Photoshop Document)
tools.description: Photoshop's native layered format: keeps layers, groups, masks, layer styles, adjustment and fill layers, smart objects, type, paths, channels, guides, layer comps, colour profile and XMP metadata at 1/8/16/32 bits per channel. Limited to 30,000 x 30,000 px and 2 GB; larger documents must use PSB. Read by most Adobe apps and many third-party tools via the flattened composite that Maximize Compatibility embeds.
tools.usage: File > Save / Save As... > Photoshop (*.PSD, *.PDD, *.PSDT)   |   PhotoshopSaveOptions {layers, alphaChannels, annotations, spotColors, embedColorProfile}

parameters.name: Layers / Alpha Channels / Spot Colors / Annotations
parameters.description: Save As checkboxes; unticking Layers flattens the copy.

parameters.name: Maximize Compatibility
parameters.description: Preferences > File Handling; embeds a composite so Lightroom, InDesign and older versions can render the file.

tools.notes: PSD compression is RLE (can be disabled in File Handling for faster saves). Cloud documents use a .psdc container but are PSDs internally. The .psdt extension marks a template opened as a new untitled document.

tools.name: PSB (Large Document Format)
tools.description: The same feature set as PSD but with the 300,000 x 300,000 px canvas limit and no 2 GB file cap, using 64-bit offsets. Required for gigapixel panoramas, print-size matte paintings and any document that exceeds the PSD limits; Photoshop offers it automatically when a document is too large to save as PSD.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > Large Document Format (*.PSB)   |   Use PhotoshopSaveOptions with a .psb file name (or LargeDocumentSaveOptions in older references)
tools.example: app.activeDocument.saveAs(new File("C:/out/giant.psb"), new PhotoshopSaveOptions(), false, Extension.LOWERCASE);
tools.notes: Not readable by most non-Adobe software or by Lightroom Classic before 2019 (which reads PSB up to 65,000 px). Embedded Smart Object contents are always stored as PSB regardless of the parent format.

tools.name: Photoshop PDF
tools.description: PDF written by Photoshop can optionally preserve full Photoshop editing capability (layers, type, effects) inside the PDF while also containing a print-ready page, using Adobe PDF presets (High Quality Print, PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-4, Smallest File Size). Use it for single-image print hand-off with vector type and for password-protected proofs; the Open dialog imports any PDF page or its embedded images at a chosen resolution.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > Photoshop PDF (*.PDF, *.PDP)   |   PDFSaveOptions {presetFile, PDFCompatibility, preserveEditing, jpegQuality, layers, embedThumbnail, ...}   |   Open: PDFOpenOptions {page, resolution, mode, cropPage, usePageNumber}

parameters.name: Adobe PDF Preset
parameters.description: High Quality Print, PDF/X-1a:2001, PDF/X-3:2002, PDF/X-4:2008, Press Quality, Smallest File Size.

parameters.name: Preserve Photoshop Editing Capabilities
parameters.description: Embeds the PSD data (much larger file).

parameters.name: Compression
parameters.description: ZIP, JPEG (quality), JPEG2000 with downsampling options.

parameters.name: Security
parameters.description: Open and permissions passwords, printing/editing restrictions.

tools.notes: Multi-page PDFs come from File > Automate > PDF Presentation or Bridge Output, not from Save As. Opening a PDF rasterises it unless placed as a Smart Object (File > Place Embedded).

tools.name: TIFF
tools.description: The lossless interchange format for print and archiving: 8/16/32-bit, RGB/CMYK/Lab/Grayscale/Indexed/Bitmap, alpha channels, transparency, layers (Photoshop-specific), spot channels, ICC profiles and up to 4 GB. Compression options are None, LZW, ZIP or JPEG for the image and RLE/ZIP for layer data; byte order IBM PC or Macintosh. Layered TIFFs open fully in Photoshop but appear flattened elsewhere.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > TIFF (*.TIF, *.TIFF)   |   TiffSaveOptions {imageCompression (NONE|LZW|ZIP|JPEG), jpegQuality, layers, layerCompression (RLE|ZIP), transparency, alphaChannels, byteOrder, saveImagePyramid, embedColorProfile}

parameters.name: Image Compression
parameters.description: NONE (fastest, largest), LZW (lossless, ~40 % smaller), ZIP (lossless, best for 16-bit), JPEG (lossy).

parameters.name: Pixel Order
parameters.description: Interleaved (RGBRGB) or Per Channel (RRGGBB, slightly faster in Photoshop).

parameters.name: Save Image Pyramid
parameters.description: Multi-resolution tiles for apps that support them.

parameters.name: Save Transparency / Layers / Layer Compression
parameters.description: Keep alpha transparency; include layers (RLE or ZIP compressed) or discard them.

tools.notes: Preferences > File Handling > 'Ask Before Saving Layered TIFF Files' guards against oversized layered TIFFs. Lightroom edits Photoshop TIFFs losslessly; JPEG-compressed TIFFs are not supported by many RIPs.

tools.name: JPEG
tools.description: Lossy 8-bit RGB/CMYK/Grayscale format for photographs on the web and in print delivery; no layers, alpha or transparency. Photoshop offers quality 0-12, Baseline/Optimized/Progressive encoding and ICC embedding in Save As / Save a Copy, and a 0-100 scale in Export As. Also stores EXIF, IPTC and XMP metadata and, optionally, Content Credentials.
tools.usage: File > Save a Copy... > JPEG (*.JPG, *.JPEG, *.JPE)   |   File > Export > Export As > JPG   |   JPEGSaveOptions {quality 0-12, formatOptions (STANDARDBASELINE|OPTIMIZEDBASELINE|PROGRESSIVE), scans, matte, embedColorProfile}

parameters.name: Quality
parameters.description: 0-12 (Save As) or 1-100 % (Export As); 10/80 % is a good default, 12/100 % is near-lossless but large.

parameters.name: Format Options
parameters.description: Baseline Standard, Baseline Optimized (smaller, universal support today), Progressive (3-5 scans).

parameters.name: Matte
parameters.description: Colour that replaces transparency (None = white).

tools.example:
var o = new JPEGSaveOptions(); o.quality = 9; o.formatOptions = FormatOptions.OPTIMIZEDBASELINE; o.embedColorProfile = true;
app.activeDocument.saveAs(new File("C:/out/photo.jpg"), o, true, Extension.LOWERCASE);
tools.notes: Since 22.4 JPEG is offered via Save a Copy (not Save As) for layered documents unless 'Enable legacy Save As' is on in File Handling. 16-bit documents must be converted to 8-bit first (Save a Copy does it silently). Chroma subsampling is 4:2:0 below quality 7 and 4:4:4 at 7+.

tools.name: JPEG 2000
tools.description: Wavelet-based successor to JPEG (.jpf/.jpx/.jp2/.j2c/.j2k/.jpc) supporting lossless or lossy compression, 8/16-bit, transparency and alpha channels, embedded profiles and progressive decoding. Rarely used outside archives, medical and geospatial imaging, but Photoshop still ships the plug-in.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > JPEG 2000 (*.JPF, *.JPX, *.JP2, *.J2C, *.J2K, *.JPC)

parameters.name: Lossless / Quality
parameters.description: Tick Lossless or set a quality/file-size target.

parameters.name: Include Transparency / Metadata / Color Settings
parameters.description: Alpha and metadata options.

parameters.name: JP2 Compatible
parameters.description: Write the plain ISO .jp2 container for maximum compatibility.

tools.example: Save a 16-bit archival scan as JPEG 2000 with Lossless ticked for roughly half the size of an uncompressed TIFF.
tools.notes: Not available in Export As or Save for Web. Not scriptable through the DOM (Action Manager only).

tools.name: PNG
tools.description: Lossless 8- or 16-bit RGB/Grayscale format with 8-bit alpha transparency, the standard for UI assets, logos and screenshots. Save As offers compression None/Smallest and Interlaced; Export As adds PNG-8 (palette) vs PNG-24, transparency and 'Smaller File (8-bit)' options; Quick Export as PNG is the one-click route. PNG carries XMP metadata and Content Credentials but no CMYK, layers or paths.
tools.usage: File > Save a Copy... > PNG (*.PNG, *.PNS)   |   File > Export > Quick Export as PNG / Export As > PNG   |   PNGSaveOptions {compression 0-9, interlaced}   |   ExportOptionsSaveForWeb {format: SaveDocumentType.PNG, PNG8, transparency, ...}

parameters.name: Compression
parameters.description: Save As: None (fastest) or Smallest/Slowest; scripting 0-9 (size differences are modest).

parameters.name: Interlaced
parameters.description: Adam7 progressive display; larger file.

parameters.name: PNG-8 / PNG-24 (Export As)
parameters.description: Palette (up to 256 colours, 1-bit or dithered transparency) vs full colour with 8-bit alpha.

tools.example:
var o = new PNGSaveOptions(); o.compression = 6; o.interlaced = false;
app.activeDocument.saveAs(new File("C:/out/icon.png"), o, true, Extension.LOWERCASE);
tools.notes: 16-bit documents save as 16-bit PNG (not all viewers support it); Export As always writes 8-bit. PNG does not store resolution reliably for print. .PNS is the stereo-pair variant.

tools.name: GIF
tools.description: 8-bit indexed-colour format (up to 256 colours, 1-bit transparency, optional frame animation) still used for simple animations and stickers. Save As converts to Indexed Color with palette, dither and matte options; Export As and Save for Web (Legacy) build animated GIFs from Timeline frames with looping control.
tools.usage: File > Save a Copy... > GIF (*.GIF)   |   File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) > GIF (for animation, Looping Options)   |   GIFSaveOptions {colors, dither, ditherAmount, forced, interlaced, matte, palette, preserveExactColors, transparency}

parameters.name: Palette
parameters.description: Exact, Local/Master Perceptual, Selective, Adaptive, Web, Custom, Windows/Mac system.

parameters.name: Colors / Dither
parameters.description: 2-256 colours; None, Diffusion (%), Pattern, Noise.

parameters.name: Transparency / Matte
parameters.description: 1-bit transparency; matte colour for anti-aliased edges.

parameters.name: Looping Options (animation)
parameters.description: Once, Forever, Other (count) - Save for Web only.

tools.example:
1. Window > Timeline > Create Frame Animation, add frames and delays.
2. File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy): GIF, 128 colours, Diffusion 80 %, Looping Forever, Save.
tools.notes: Animated GIF export is not available via Save As/Save a Copy - only Save for Web (Legacy) and Export As. Consider APNG/WebP/video for higher quality.

tools.name: WebP
tools.description: Google's web format supporting lossy and lossless compression, 8-bit alpha transparency and metadata, typically 25-35 % smaller than JPEG at similar quality. Native support arrived in Photoshop 23.2 (February 2022) for Open, Place, Save As/Save a Copy and Export As, without a plug-in.
tools.usage: File > Save a Copy... > WebP (*.WEBP)   |   File > Export > Export As > WebP (23.2+)

parameters.name: Lossy / Lossless
parameters.description: Lossless keeps every pixel (larger); Lossy exposes a Quality slider 0-100.

parameters.name: Include XMP metadata / ICC profile / EXIF
parameters.description: Metadata checkboxes in the WebP options dialog.

tools.example: Open a PNG hero image, File > Save a Copy > WebP, Lossy quality 80, tick Include ICC profile.
tools.notes: 8-bit RGB/Grayscale only; convert 16-bit documents first. Animated WebP is not supported. Not exposed as a Save option class in ExtendScript - use Action Manager (recorded 'save' descriptor with 'WebPFormat').

tools.name: HEIF / HEIC
tools.description: The High Efficiency Image Format used by iPhone and modern cameras (HEVC-coded, 8/10-bit, with depth maps). Photoshop opens HEIC/HEIF (routing them through Camera Raw when JPEG/HEIC handling is enabled) and can save HEIF via Save As; on Windows the Microsoft HEIF Image Extensions and HEVC Video Extensions must be installed first.
tools.usage: File > Open / Save As... > HEIF (*.HEIC, *.HEIF)   |   Camera Raw: Preferences > File Handling > JPEG, HEIC and TIFF Handling

parameters.name: Codecs (Windows)
parameters.description: Install 'HEIF Image Extensions' and 'HEVC Video Extensions' from the Microsoft Store.

parameters.name: Depth map
parameters.description: iPhone portrait HEICs expose a depth channel that Lens Blur / Select Subject can use via Camera Raw.

tools.example: Set Camera Raw Preferences > File Handling to open all supported HEICs, then File > Open an iPhone photo to edit it raw-style with HDR headroom.
tools.notes: Saving HEIF is 8- or 10-bit lossy only; alpha is not supported. macOS supports HEIC natively (10.13+).

tools.name: AVIF
tools.description: AV1-based image format (AOMedia) delivering around 50 % smaller files than JPEG at equal quality with 8/10/12-bit depth, HDR, wide gamut and alpha. Photoshop 26.8 (June 2025) added native AVIF open and save through Save As / Save a Copy; it is not offered by Export As or Save for Web (Legacy).
tools.usage: File > Open / Save a Copy... > AVIF (*.AVIF)  (Photoshop 26.8 and later)

parameters.name: Quality
parameters.description: Lossy quality slider; lossless option where offered.

parameters.name: Bit depth
parameters.description: 8-bit from 8-bit documents; 10/12-bit HDR output from 16/32-bit HDR documents.

tools.example: Image > Mode > 16 Bits/Channel with an HDR display profile, then File > Save a Copy > AVIF for an HDR web image.
tools.notes: Before 26.8 a third-party plug-in (e.g. 0xC0000054/avif-format) was required. Browser support is universal in current Chrome, Firefox and Safari 16+.

tools.name: JPEG XL
tools.description: The JPEG committee's modern format (.jxl) with lossless or lossy modes, up to 32-bit float, HDR, alpha, animation and lossless recompression of legacy JPEGs. Photoshop 26.8 (June 2025) added native open and Save As / Save a Copy support alongside AVIF.
tools.usage: File > Open / Save a Copy... > JPEG XL (*.JXL)  (Photoshop 26.8 and later)

parameters.name: Lossless / Quality
parameters.description: Lossless mode or a lossy quality/effort setting.

tools.example: Save a 16-bit master as lossless JPEG XL to cut archive size versus TIFF while keeping full fidelity.
tools.notes: Browser support is limited (Safari 17+; not Chrome), so use JXL for archives and internal pipelines rather than public web delivery. Not available in Export As.

tools.name: SVG (import and export)
tools.description: Scalable Vector Graphics can be opened (rasterised at a chosen size), placed as a Smart Object (stays vector, re-rasterised on transform), or generated by Export As / Generate Image Assets from shape, type and pixel layers. Exported SVG keeps shape layers as paths, type as text or outlines and embeds any raster content as base64 images.
tools.usage: File > Open (rasterise dialog) / File > Place Embedded (vector Smart Object)   |   File > Export > Export As > SVG   |   Generator: name a layer 'icon.svg'

parameters.name: Rasterize SVG dialog
parameters.description: Width, Height, Resolution, Constrain Proportions, Mode when opening.

parameters.name: Export As > SVG
parameters.description: Exports selected layers/artboards; complex effects are rasterised inside the SVG.

tools.example: Draw a logo with the shape tools, select the layers, File > Export > Export As, format SVG, Export.
tools.notes: Placed SVGs referencing external fonts or CSS may not render identically; convert type to outlines in Illustrator first. SVG export is not offered for Smart Filters or 3D layers.

tools.name: DNG (Digital Negative)
tools.description: Adobe's open raw container: stores the sensor data (or a linear demosaiced image) plus metadata, an optional embedded JPEG preview and, in newer versions, Enhance/Denoise output and lossy raw compression. Photoshop opens DNG through Camera Raw; the free Adobe DNG Converter turns proprietary raws into DNG for older software.
tools.usage: File > Open (Camera Raw dialog) > Save Image... > Format DNG   |   CameraRAWOpenOptions for scripted opening

parameters.name: Compatibility
parameters.description: Camera Raw 2.4 / 4.1 / 5.4 / 6.6 / 7.1 and later, and 11.2 and later (Enhanced/lossy).

parameters.name: JPEG Preview / Embed Fast Load Data / Use Lossy Compression / Embed Original Raw File
parameters.description: DNG Converter and Camera Raw save options.

tools.notes: Denoise and Super Resolution in Camera Raw write new '<name>-Enhanced-NR.dng' files. Edits are stored as XMP inside the DNG (no sidecar).

tools.name: Camera raw formats (CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF, RW2, PEF, DNG...)
tools.description: Proprietary sensor-data files from every major camera maker, opened exclusively through the Camera Raw plug-in (which must be updated for new camera models). Raw files are never overwritten: edits live in .xmp sidecars or the Camera Raw database, and the developed image is opened into Photoshop as a normal (or Smart Object) layer at the workflow bit depth and colour space.
tools.usage: File > Open > raw file > Camera Raw dialog > Open / Open Object   |   app.open(File, CameraRAWOpenOptions)

parameters.name: Workflow Options (Camera Raw)
parameters.description: Color space, depth (8/16-bit), image sizing, sharpening for output, Open in Photoshop as Smart Objects.

parameters.name: Sidecar XMP
parameters.description: Camera Raw Preferences > General > Save image settings in Sidecar .xmp files.

tools.example: Shift-click Open in Camera Raw (Open Object) to place the raw as a Smart Object so Filter > Camera Raw can be re-edited later.
tools.notes: Unsupported new cameras: update Camera Raw (Creative Cloud app) or convert with Adobe DNG Converter. Vendor 'compressed raw' variants (e.g. CR3 C-RAW, Sony lossless) are listed on the supported-cameras page.

tools.name: Photoshop EPS
tools.description: Encapsulated PostScript for legacy print workflows: a flattened 8-bit raster (RGB, CMYK, Grayscale, Duotone, Bitmap) with optional clipping path, halftone screen and transfer function, plus a TIFF preview. Superseded by PDF and TIFF but still requested by some RIPs and for Duotone/Bitmap art with clipping paths. Opening an EPS/AI/PostScript file rasterises it.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > Photoshop EPS (*.EPS)   |   EPSSaveOptions {preview, encoding (ASCII|BINARY|JPEG...), halftoneScreen, transferFunction, psColorManagement, vectorData, interpolation, transparentWhites}   |   Open: EPSOpenOptions {width, height, resolution, mode, antiAlias, constrainProportions}

parameters.name: Preview
parameters.description: None, TIFF (1 bit/8 bit), Macintosh (legacy).

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: ASCII, ASCII85, Binary, JPEG (Low-Maximum quality).

parameters.name: Include Halftone Screen / Transfer Function / Vector Data
parameters.description: Prepress extras; Vector Data preserves shape/type outlines once (lost on reopen).

parameters.name: Transparent Whites (Bitmap mode)
parameters.description: Treat white as transparent.

tools.example: Image > Mode > Duotone, then File > Save As > Photoshop EPS with Include Halftone Screen for a two-colour press job.
tools.notes: Photoshop DCS 1.0/2.0 are EPS variants that split CMYK plus spot channels into separations (DCS2SaveOptions). Placing an Illustrator .ai keeps it vector as a Smart Object; opening it rasterises.

tools.name: BMP
tools.description: Windows bitmap: 1/4/8/16/24/32-bit uncompressed (or RLE) raster with no layers or colour management, used by some embedded systems, game tools and Windows UI resources. Photoshop writes Windows or OS/2 headers, optional RLE compression for 4/8-bit and 'Flip Row Order' for bottom-up layouts.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > BMP (*.BMP, *.RLE, *.DIB)   |   BMPSaveOptions {osType (WINDOWS|OS2), depth (BMPDepthType.ONE...THIRTYTWO), rleCompression, flipRowOrder, alphaChannels}

parameters.name: File Format
parameters.description: Windows or OS/2.

parameters.name: Depth
parameters.description: 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 bit (32 includes alpha via Advanced Modes).

parameters.name: Compress (RLE) / Flip Row Order
parameters.description: Optional RLE; row order for tools that expect top-down data.

tools.example:
var o = new BMPSaveOptions(); o.depth = BMPDepthType.TWENTYFOUR; o.osType = OperatingSystem.WINDOWS;
app.activeDocument.saveAs(new File("C:/out/splash.bmp"), o, true);
tools.notes: Alpha in 32-bit BMP is honoured only by some readers. 8-bit documents only; RGB or Indexed.

tools.name: Targa (TGA)
tools.description: Truevision TGA: 16/24/32-bit RGB raster with a single 8-bit alpha channel and optional RLE compression, historically the texture format of game engines and VFX. Photoshop stores the first alpha channel (not layer transparency) in the 32-bit alpha, so add an alpha channel before saving.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > Targa (*.TGA, *.VDA, *.ICB, *.VST)   |   TargaSaveOptions {resolution (TargaBitsPerPixels.SIXTEEN|TWENTYFOUR|THIRTYTWO), rleCompression, alphaChannels}

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: 16, 24 or 32 bits/pixel (32 = 24 + alpha channel).

parameters.name: Compress (RLE)
parameters.description: Lossless run-length compression.

tools.example: Channels panel > New Channel (paste the mask), then Save As Targa 32 bits/pixel with Alpha Channels ticked.
tools.notes: Transparency of a layer is not written unless converted to an alpha channel (Ctrl-click layer thumbnail > Select > Save Selection). 8-bit documents only.

tools.name: OpenEXR
tools.description: ILM's floating-point HDR format used by 3D renderers and compositors: 16-bit half or 32-bit float per channel, lossless/lossy compression (PIZ, ZIP, RLE, PXR24, B44, DWAA/DWAB), arbitrary channels/AOVs and metadata. Photoshop opens EXR as a 32-bit/channel document (single RGBA layer; extra render passes are not exposed) and saves 32-bit documents back to EXR with a choice of compression and alpha handling.
tools.usage: File > Open (32-bit document) / Save As... > OpenEXR (*.EXR)  (document must be 32 Bits/Channel)

parameters.name: Alpha Channel
parameters.description: None, Straight (unpremultiplied) or Premultiplied; Photoshop's layer transparency is written straight.

parameters.name: Compression
parameters.description: None, RLE, ZIP, ZIPS, PIZ, PXR24, B44, B44A, DWAA, DWAB.

parameters.name: Color Space (open)
parameters.description: Assumed linear; assign an ICC (e.g. Linear ProPhoto/ACEScg) via Edit > Assign Profile after opening.

tools.example: Open beauty.exr, View > 32-bit Preview Options to set Exposure, paint fixes on a new layer, File > Save As > OpenEXR with PIZ compression.
tools.notes: Multi-layer/AOV EXRs need the free 'Exr-IO' plug-in or a compositor. Most filters and adjustments are unavailable at 32-bit; Image > Mode > 16 Bits/Channel invokes HDR Toning.

tools.name: Radiance HDR (.hdr)
tools.description: The RGBE format of Greg Ward's Radiance renderer: 32-bit float radiance stored as 8-bit mantissas plus a shared exponent, the classic container for HDRI environment maps and light probes. Photoshop opens and saves it for 32-bit documents; Merge to HDR Pro can write it directly.
tools.usage: File > Open / Save As... > Radiance (*.HDR, *.RGBE, *.XYZE)  (32-bit documents)
tools.example: File > Automate > Merge to HDR Pro on a bracketed set, Mode 32 Bit, then Save As > Radiance for use as an environment map in a 3D application.
tools.notes: No alpha channel or layers. Lower precision than OpenEXR half-float in the shadows; prefer EXR for compositing.

tools.name: DICOM
tools.description: The medical-imaging standard (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound); Photoshop opens single files or whole series as frames (N-up grid or layers), reads the patient/study header as metadata, supports 8/16-bit grey and RGB, windowing (level/width) on import and can anonymise the header. File > Scripts > Load Multiple DICOM Files builds a stack for volume rendering or animation.
tools.usage: File > Open > DICOM (*.DCM, *.DC3, *.DIC)   |   File > Scripts > Load Multiple DICOM Files...   |   DICOMOpenOptions {anonymize, columns, rows, reverse, showOverlays, windowLevel, windowWidth}

parameters.name: Frame Import
parameters.description: Import Frames as Layers, N-Up Configuration (rows x columns), Import as Volume (3D, removed with 3D).

parameters.name: Window Level / Width
parameters.description: Grey-level mapping applied on import.

parameters.name: Anonymize / Show Overlays
parameters.description: Strip patient data; show burnt-in annotations.

tools.example: File > Open series001.dcm, select all frames, Import Frames as Layers, Anonymize, then Window > Timeline > Create Frame Animation > Make Frames From Layers.
tools.notes: Saving as DICOM writes 8-bit only and keeps the header (File > File Info > DICOM tab). Not a substitute for a clinical viewer; use for presentation/illustration.

tools.name: IFF, PCX, Pixar, Scitex CT and Portable Bit Map
tools.description: Legacy raster formats Photoshop still reads and writes for interoperability: IFF (Amiga/Maya .iff/.tdi, with alpha), PCX (ZSoft PC Paintbrush, 8/24-bit RLE), Pixar (.pxr, RenderMan textures), Scitex CT (.sct, high-end CMYK prepress scanners) and Portable Bit Map (.pbm/.pgm/.ppm/.pnm/.pfm - the Netpbm family used by scientific and command-line tools). All are flat, single-layer, mostly 8-bit files.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > IFF Format / PCX / Pixar / Scitex CT / Portable Bit Map   |   PixarSaveOptions, PCXSaveOptions, SGIRGBSaveOptions (some via Action Manager only)

parameters.name: Portable Bit Map
parameters.description: Reads/writes ASCII or binary PNM up to 16-bit; useful to exchange with ImageMagick/Netpbm without a JPEG round trip.

parameters.name: Scitex CT
parameters.description: CMYK or Grayscale only; no alpha.

tools.example: File > Save As > Portable Bit Map to feed a Grayscale document to a command-line OCR tool that only reads .pgm.
tools.notes: PICT, PICT Resource, Photo CD and several others were removed in CC 2015-2018; see the 'Supported file formats' page for the current list of your version.

tools.name: Photoshop Raw (headerless .raw)
tools.description: Not camera raw: a headerless dump of pixel bytes (interleaved or per-channel) with an optional header of N bytes, used to exchange data with scientific instruments, custom software and early scanners. On open you must specify width, height, channel count, depth, byte order and header size; on save you choose the header size and channel order. Any 8/16-bit mode without layers can be written.
tools.usage: File > Open > Photoshop Raw (*.RAW) > Photoshop Raw Options dialog   |   RawFormatOpenOptions {width, height, channelNumber, interleaveChannels, headerSize, bitsPerChannel, byteOrder, retainHeader}   |   RawSaveOptions {fileCreator, fileType, spotColors, alphaChannels}

parameters.name: Dimensions / Channels / Depth
parameters.description: Width, height, count of channels, 8 or 16 bits, Interleaved checkbox.

parameters.name: Byte Order
parameters.description: IBM PC (little-endian) or Macintosh (big-endian) for 16-bit data.

parameters.name: Header
parameters.description: Bytes to skip before pixel data; Retain When Saving.

tools.notes: The Open dialog's 'Guess' button tries to infer dimensions from the file size. Do not confuse with Camera Raw formats.

tools.name: Cineon and DPX
tools.description: Kodak Cineon (.cin) and its SMPTE successor DPX (.dpx) hold 10-bit logarithmic film-scan data frame by frame for motion-picture work. Photoshop opens them into 16-bit RGB (with log-to-linear conversion options) and saves back to Cineon 10-bit log, which lets VFX artists paint on individual scanned frames.
tools.usage: File > Open / Save As... > Cineon (*.CIN, *.SDPX, *.DPX, *.FIDO)

parameters.name: Cineon options
parameters.description: Log-to-linear conversion: white/black points, gamma, and 'Keep as Log'.

tools.example: Open shot_0001.dpx, retouch wires on a duplicate layer, flatten, File > Save As > Cineon to return the frame to the compositor.
tools.notes: Processing image sequences frame by frame is better done with File > Import > Video Frames to Layers or via Batch on a folder of DPX files.

tools.name: Video and image-sequence formats (MOV, MP4, AVI, image sequences)
tools.description: Photoshop imports QuickTime MOV, MP4/H.264, AVI, MPEG-1/2/4, and numbered image sequences (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, DPX...) as video layers or frame layers, and renders the Timeline back out through File > Export > Render Video using Adobe Media Encoder presets (H.264, QuickTime, DPX/PNG/JPEG sequences, animated GIF via Save for Web).
tools.usage: File > Open (video file) / Layer > Video Layers > New Video Layer from File / File > Import > Video Frames to Layers   |   File > Export > Render Video...

parameters.name: Render Video > Format
parameters.description: H.264 (presets High/Medium/Low, YouTube/Vimeo sizes), QuickTime (Animation, ProRes on macOS), Photoshop Image Sequence (JPEG/PNG/TIFF/DPX/Targa...).

parameters.name: Range / Frame Rate / Render Options
parameters.description: All frames, in/out points, work area; document frame rate; alpha (straight/premultiplied), 3D quality (legacy).

parameters.name: Video Frames to Layers
parameters.description: Range, Limit To Every N Frames, Make Frame Animation.

tools.example: File > Import > Video Frames to Layers on a 3-second MP4, Limit To Every 2 Frames, Make Frame Animation; add a Curves layer on top; File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) > GIF.
tools.notes: H.264 with alpha is not possible; use PNG/ProRes 4444 sequences. Some codecs require QuickTime-free decoding available since CC 2018; unsupported codecs show a 'Could not complete... file format module cannot parse' error.

tools.name: 3D formats (OBJ, 3DS, DAE, KMZ, U3D) - deprecated
tools.description: Photoshop Extended/CC 3D features could open and export Wavefront OBJ, 3D Studio 3DS, Collada DAE, Google Earth KMZ and U3D meshes, and print to STL/OBJ. Adobe deprecated the 3D engine in Photoshop 22.5 (August 2021) and removed it from the 2024 release onward; files with 3D layers open with the layers rasterised or unavailable. Use Substance 3D Stager / Adobe Dimension for 3D work.
tools.usage: Legacy: 3D > New 3D Layer from File... / 3D > Export 3D Layer... (Photoshop 22.x and earlier, or with 'Enable legacy 3D' where offered)
tools.example: To recover an old PSD with a 3D layer, open it in Photoshop 22.x (installable from the Creative Cloud app's 'Other versions' list) and 3D > Export 3D Layer to OBJ.
tools.notes: Related removals: 3D Material Drop / Eyedropper tools, Lighting Effects (3D version), Extrude to 3D for type, Load Multiple DICOM 'as volume'.

tools.name: ABR (brush presets)
tools.description: Brush preset file holding brush tips (sampled or computed), brush settings (shape dynamics, scattering, texture, dual brush, transfer, wet edges, colour dynamics), tool colour (optional) and group structure. Photoshop 2018+ writes version-6 ABR with groups; older versions read only tip-and-settings ABRs. Thousands of third-party brush packs use it.
tools.usage: Brushes panel menu > Import Brushes... / Export Selected Brushes...   |   Edit > Presets > Preset Manager (legacy, for older ABR)   |   File > Open on an .abr also imports

parameters.name: Import Brushes
parameters.description: Adds the file's brushes as a new group in the Brushes panel.

parameters.name: Export Selected Brushes
parameters.description: Writes the selected brushes/groups to a new ABR.

tools.example: Double-click a downloaded 'Kyle Ultimate Inking.abr' to import it; the brushes appear as a group in Window > Brushes.
tools.notes: Brush tips are limited to 5000 x 5000 px. Tool Presets (.tpl) store the full tool state including brush and are separate from ABR.

tools.name: ATN (action sets)
tools.description: Actions panel set file: one set containing any number of recorded actions with their steps, dialog toggles, conditionals and inserted stops/menu items. ATN files are the unit of exchange for automation (Batch, Droplets, Image Processor, Photoshop API photoshopActions) and are loaded by double-click or the panel menu.
tools.usage: Actions panel menu > Load Actions... / Save Actions... (select a set first) / Replace Actions...   |   Photoshop API: /v2/execute-actions with an .atn input   |   COM/ExtendScript: app.doAction(actionName, setName)

parameters.name: Save Actions
parameters.description: Saves the selected set; Ctrl+Alt-click Save Actions writes a plain-text listing (.txt) of the steps.

parameters.name: Button Mode
parameters.description: Panel view that turns each action into a coloured button.

tools.example: Select the set 'Web Export', Actions panel menu > Save Actions..., store 'Web Export.atn' in a shared folder; teammates use Load Actions.
tools.notes: Actions reference layers by name/order and fonts by name, so they are only as portable as their assumptions. Files from newer versions may fail in older ones.

tools.name: ASL (layer styles)
tools.description: Layer style preset file: each style bundles a complete set of layer effects (drop shadow, bevel, overlays, stroke...) and optionally the layer blend mode/opacity, ready to apply from the Styles panel with one click. Used to distribute text-effect packs and UI kits.
tools.usage: Styles panel menu > Import Styles... / Export Selected Styles...   |   ArtLayer.applyStyle("style name") applies a loaded style by name

parameters.name: Include Layer Effects / Include Layer Blending Options
parameters.description: New Style dialog options controlling what the preset stores.

tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.applyStyle("Chrome - Sunset");   // style must already be loaded in the Styles panel
tools.notes: Styles scale with document resolution only if 'Scale Effects' is used after applying; Layer > Layer Style > Scale Effects.

tools.name: ACO and ASE (swatches) and ACT (colour tables)
tools.description: ACO is Photoshop's swatch file (RGB/CMYK/Lab/HSB colours with names, plus groups in v2 files); ASE (Adobe Swatch Exchange) is the cross-app format shared with Illustrator, InDesign and Creative Cloud Libraries; ACT is a flat 256-entry colour table used by Indexed Color mode (Image > Mode > Color Table) and Save for Web palettes.
tools.usage: Swatches panel menu > Import Swatches... (.aco/.ase/.act) / Export Selected Swatches... (.aco) / Export Swatches for Exchange... (.ase)   |   Image > Mode > Color Table > Load/Save (.act)
tools.example: Export the brand palette with Export Swatches for Exchange, then import the .ase into Illustrator and Creative Cloud Libraries.
tools.notes: ASE does not carry swatch groups from Photoshop; ACO v2 does. Legacy swatches are available from the panel menu > Legacy Swatches.

tools.name: GRD (gradients)
tools.description: Gradient preset file with colour and opacity stops, midpoints, gradient type (Solid or Noise) and, since 2020, group structure. Used by the Gradient tool, Gradient fill layers, Gradient Map adjustments and Gradient Overlay styles; Photoshop 2020+ also reads gradient groups imported from the Gradients panel.
tools.usage: Gradients panel menu > Import Gradients... / Export Selected Gradients...   |   Gradient Editor > Load / Save (legacy)
tools.example: Gradients panel > select the 'Brand' group > panel menu > Export Selected Gradients... > brand.grd.
tools.notes: Noise gradients store their random seed so they reload identically. The scripting DOM has no gradient object; apply gradients via Action Manager descriptors.

tools.name: PAT (patterns)
tools.description: Pattern preset file holding one or more raster tiles (with names and groups) used by Edit > Fill > Pattern, Pattern fill layers, Pattern Overlay, the Pattern Stamp and Healing Brush 'pattern' modes. Define new tiles with Edit > Define Pattern from a rectangular selection; View > Pattern Preview shows how they tile.
tools.usage: Patterns panel menu > Import Patterns... / Export Selected Patterns...   |   Edit > Define Pattern...
tools.example: Select a 256 x 256 seamless tile, Edit > Define Pattern 'paper', then Patterns panel > Export Selected Patterns to share paper.pat.
tools.notes: Tiles are stored uncompressed, so large patterns make big PAT files. Legacy Patterns are under the panel menu > Legacy Patterns and More.

tools.name: CSH (custom shapes)
tools.description: Custom Shape preset file: vector paths (with names and groups) available to the Custom Shape tool and the Shapes panel. Create shapes with Edit > Define Custom Shape from any path or shape layer; imported CSH files appear as a group.
tools.usage: Shapes panel menu > Import Shapes... / Export Selected Shapes...   |   Edit > Define Custom Shape...
tools.example: Draw an icon with the Pen tool, Edit > Define Custom Shape 'pin', then export the group as icons.csh.
tools.notes: Shapes are resolution-independent. Legacy shapes (arrows, symbols) load via panel menu > Legacy Shapes and More.

tools.name: TPL (tool presets)
tools.description: Tool preset file storing the complete options-bar state of a tool (brush tip and settings, blend mode, opacity, flow, colour if included, crop ratios, type settings...). Presets appear in the options-bar preset picker and the Tool Presets panel; saving and loading .tpl files moves them between machines.
tools.usage: Window > Tool Presets > panel menu > Load Tool Presets... / Save Tool Presets...   |   options bar > Tool Preset picker > gear > New Tool Preset

parameters.name: Include Color
parameters.description: Store the foreground colour with a painting-tool preset.

parameters.name: Current Tool Only
parameters.description: Panel filter.

tools.example: Set the Crop tool to 16:9 at 300 ppi, options bar preset picker > New Tool Preset 'Crop 16x9 print', then Save Tool Presets to crop.tpl.
tools.notes: Edit > Presets > Export/Import Presets moves all preset types (tools, brushes, actions...) at once.

tools.name: Adjustment preset files (ACV, ALV, AHU, ACB, AMP, ADO, 3DL/CUBE LUTs)
tools.description: Per-adjustment preset formats saved from the adjustment dialogs and Properties panel menus: .acv Curves, .amp arbitrary Curves map, .alv Levels, .ahu Hue/Saturation, .acb Color Balance, .ado Duotone, .asv Selective Color, .ape Exposure, .chn Channel Mixer, .blw Black & White, .shh Shadows/Highlights, and the LUT formats (.3dl, .cube, .look, .csp) read by Color Lookup and exported by File > Export > Color Lookup Tables. They let a look be reused across files, in Batch actions and in other applications.
tools.usage: Properties panel (adjustment) menu > Save <Adjustment> Preset... / Load <Adjustment> Preset...   |   File > Export > Color Lookup Tables...

parameters.name: Color Lookup Tables export
parameters.description: Description, Copyright, Quality (Grid Points), Formats 3DL / CUBE / CSP / ICC Profile.

tools.example: Build a grade with Curves + Color Balance layers over a Background, then File > Export > Color Lookup Tables (CUBE, 33 points); apply anywhere with a Color Lookup adjustment layer.
tools.notes: Camera Raw presets are .xmp files, not these. LUT export requires a Background layer with the adjustments stacked above it.

tools.name: JSX and JSXBIN (ExtendScript files)
tools.description: ExtendScript source files (.jsx, ES3 JavaScript with Adobe extensions) and their compiled/obfuscated form (.jsxbin, produced by the ExtendScript Toolkit or the VS Code ExtendScript Debugger export). Run from File > Scripts > Browse..., from the Scripts menu when placed in Presets/Scripts, by drag-and-drop or double-click (#target photoshop), from actions (Insert Menu Item) and from COM DoJavaScriptFile.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Browse... > *.jsx / *.jsxbin   |   Presets\Scripts folder (restart to list in File > Scripts)   |   #target photoshop  /  #include "lib.jsx"

parameters.name: #target photoshop
parameters.description: Directive routing the file to Photoshop when double-clicked.

parameters.name: #include / #includepath
parameters.description: Preprocessor directives to pull in shared libraries.

parameters.name: // @script
parameters.description: Not used by Photoshop; menu name comes from the file name.

tools.notes: JSXBIN cannot be edited or inspected but runs identically. Scripts in Presets/Scripts are listed alphabetically in File > Scripts and can be assigned keyboard shortcuts via Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts (Application Menus > File > Scripts).

tools.name: PSJS (UXP script files)
tools.description: Modern JavaScript script files executed by the UXP runtime (Photoshop 23.3+): ES2020 syntax, `require('photoshop')` and `require('uxp')` modules, promises/async, and access to batchPlay and the imaging API. Run from File > Scripts > Browse..., from the Scripts menu or by double-clicking; debug by loading the containing folder in the UXP Developer Tool.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Browse... > *.psjs   |   Presets\Scripts folder   |   const { app, core } = require("photoshop");
tools.notes: A .psjs runs with plugin-like permissions declared by an optional manifest; without one it gets default file access via file pickers only. Top-level await is allowed. Cannot be called from actions in early versions; use a UXP plugin command for action recording.

tools.name: CCX (Creative Cloud plugin package)
tools.description: A zipped package (.ccx) containing a UXP (or CEP) plugin's manifest and files, the distribution format for Adobe Exchange / Creative Cloud Marketplace and for private side-loading. Double-clicking a .ccx installs it through Creative Cloud Desktop; the UXP Developer Tool's Package command creates it from a plugin folder.
tools.usage: UXP Developer Tool > plugin > ... > Package (creates .ccx)   |   Double-click .ccx > Creative Cloud Desktop installs   |   Plugins menu > Manage Plugins

parameters.name: manifest.json
parameters.description: Must declare id, version, host.minVersion and entrypoints; the id must match the Developer Distribution listing.

tools.example: In UDT click Actions > Package for 'com.example.exporter', then upload exporter_1.0.0.ccx to Adobe Developer Distribution for review.
tools.notes: Unsigned/untrusted .ccx files prompt a warning. Installed plugins live under %AppData%\Adobe\UXP\PluginsStorage (Windows).

tools.name: 8BF, 8BI, 8BE, 8BA (native plug-in modules)
tools.description: Compiled C++ plug-ins built with the Photoshop SDK: .8bf filters (appear in the Filter menu), .8bi file formats (add Open/Save formats such as third-party AVIF/EXR/DDS readers), .8be selection/export modules, .8ba automation plug-ins (File > Automate) and .8bx extensions. Installed into the Plug-ins folder and loaded at start-up; must match Photoshop's architecture (64-bit; Apple Silicon needs native or Rosetta builds).
tools.usage: Copy to C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop <version>\Plug-ins\ (or Common Files\Adobe\Plug-Ins\CC) and restart   |   Help > System Info lists loaded plug-ins
tools.example: Install the Nvidia Texture Tools .8bi to open and save DDS textures, then File > Open > DDS.
tools.notes: Hold Shift during launch to skip loading optional plug-ins when one crashes. The SDK is at developer.adobe.com/photoshop (Photoshop plugin SDK / API docs).

tools.name: CSF, PSF, KYS and MNU (colour settings, proof setups, shortcuts and menu sets)
tools.description: Small settings files that make a workstation reproducible: .csf colour settings (Edit > Color Settings > Save, synchronised through Bridge), .psf proof setups (View > Proof Setup > Custom > Save), .kys keyboard shortcut sets and .mnu menu customisations (Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts and Menus > Save Set). All live in the user's Photoshop Settings folder and can be copied between machines.
tools.usage: Edit > Color Settings... > Save... (.csf)   |   View > Proof Setup > Custom... > Save... (.psf)   |   Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts... > Save Set (.kys)   |   Edit > Menus... > Save Set (.mnu)
tools.example: Save 'Studio.csf' into Program Files\Common Files\Adobe\Color\Settings so it appears in the Color Settings preset list on every machine.
tools.notes: Keyboard shortcut sets can also be exported as an HTML summary from the dialog ('Summarize').

tools.name: ICC/ICM profiles and XMP sidecars
tools.description: Colour profiles (.icc/.icm) describe devices and working spaces and are installed system-wide (Windows: right-click > Install Profile; folder Windows\System32\spool\drivers\color); Photoshop lists them in Color Settings, Assign/Convert Profile, Proof Setup and Print. XMP sidecar files (.xmp) hold Camera Raw edits and metadata for raw files that cannot be written to, and File > File Info can export/import XMP templates for any document.
tools.usage: Install profiles at OS level > restart Photoshop   |   Camera Raw Preferences > Save image settings in Sidecar .xmp   |   File > File Info... > Export/Import (.xmp)
tools.example: Download the lab's paper profile .icc, install it, then View > Proof Setup > Custom > Device to Simulate lists it.
tools.notes: UXP `app.getColorProfiles(colorMode)` (24.1+) lists the installed profiles; ExtendScript has no equivalent (read `doc.colorProfileName` or use executeActionGet). XMP sidecars must travel with the raw file or the edits are lost.
